SUBJECT:  MONTHLY FINANCIAL REPORT – NOVEMBER 2010

The Issue

What is the status of the FY 2010-11 City budget after five months?

Analysis of Graphs

Many of the revenue figures reflect four months of activity due to timing of receipts. Total
operating revenues are 1% below expected, while general fund revenues are currently running 6%
below expected. Club concession fees remain healthy at +8%; however, development fee
performance has fallen off from October activity and are now 10% below expected for the year to
date. Although a very small percentage (1.2%) of the general fund budget, property transfer taxes
have remained more robust compared to budget than past years. We use this as one indicator of the
condition of the residential housing market. Additional information is presented under spot reports
below.

Total operating expenditures are 2% below expected with departments, except Public Works and
Insurance, at less than expected. The Insurance/Attorney item will remain in excess of budget until
late in the fiscal year because of the cost for insurance deposits paid to the CJPIA in July. None of
the budget deviation for this factor is associated with the City Attorney’s services.

Spot Reports

During the past month, we received annual reports from our property tax consultant, HDL
Companies. This vendor provides a wealth of information, including number of pre-prop 13
parcels, assessment appeal activity and property transfer/sales. All these factors are used for
property tax budget projections. For FY 2010-11, the City’s assessed values declined a modest
0.37%. Of the 88 cities in LA County, 28 experienced assessed value increases, while 60 (68%)
had drops ranging from less than -1% up to -12.% and -14% for Palmdale and Lancaster,
respectively. December is the first allocation of FY 10-11 property taxes and we will provide that
data as part of the next monthly report.

FROM:  JUDY SMITH, ASSISTANT CITY MANAGER

SUBJECT:  ONE-YEAR CONTRACT EXTENSION WITH THE CITY OF INGLEWOOD
  (ICMS) FOR PARKING CITATION PROCESSING AND AMEND
  CONTRACTED SERVICES TO INCLUDE INTERNET PAYMENT OPTION

The Issue

Shall the City Council approve a one-year extension option to the City’s existing contract with the
City of Inglewood (ICMS) for parking citation processing and amend the contracted services to
include an internet payment option?

Background

For many years, the City of Palos Verdes Estates has contracted with the City of Inglewood (ICMS)
for parking citation processing services. The most recent agreement (attached) was approved by the
City Council in December 2007 for a three year term, expiring December 31, 2010 (Article 7). The
contract includes the option for two (2) one-year extensions.

Inglewood provides contract management services, but subcontracts actual citation processing to
Duncan Solutions Processor. This firm was selected as Inglewood’s vendor after a competitive,
public process. The City’s cost for parking citation processing services under the ICMS contract
totaled ~$5,800 during FY 2009-10.

Analysis and Findings

Staff is satisfied with the services provided by ICMS and Duncan. There is an opportunity as part
of the contract extension to consider service enhancements. Staff reviewed the various service
options and requests a modification to contract services to provide an internet payment option for
parking citations.

The City currently allows credit card payment for parking citations only in person at City Hall using
a hard swipe and signature of the payee. These parameters were established in light of concerns
about security and cost. After reviewing the various options, including security issues and merchant
(credit card) service charges, staff determined the most cost effective means to provide this option is
to allow payments via a secure site offered by Duncan and using their merchant account (credit card
processor) at a cost of $2.68 per citation. The City will establish a separate bank account
(+$15/month) to which Duncan will deposit proceeds on a daily basis. The separate account will
CITY COUNCIL AGENDA
DECEMBER 14, 2010
  7
 ensure that all activity related to parking is segregated from other City banking, which will also
assist Finance staff in its daily reconciliation of payment processing reports issued by Duncan.

The City Treasurer and staff view this as an important convenience and service to the public, as we
are often asked if there is another means to pay citations rather than by mail or in person. The
City’s website will provide a prominent link to the Duncan secure site and we will publicize the
service in the City newsletter.

An amended Exhibit A is attached to the Service Agreement Change Notice. Although Exhibit B is
also included as part of the Change Notice the City does not contract for any of those enumerated
services.

Alternatives Available to the City Council

  1. Approve a one-year extension to the current contract with ICMS for parking citation
  processing with no amendment to contracted services.

  2. Approve a one-year extension to the current contract and approved an amendment to the
  contracted services to provide an internet payment option for parking citations.

Recommendation

It is recommended that the City Council approve the one-year contract extension with the City of
Inglewood (ICMS) for parking citation processing services, which includes an amended “Exhibit
A” for contracted services to include an internet payment option for parking citations.

Fiscal Impact

The number of parking citations processed annually averages approximately 2,500. Staff is not able
to project at this time what percentage of violations will be paid using the internet credit card
option. Please recall, in July the City increased most parking fines by $15. Part of the increase was
to offset the additional $3.00/citation state surcharge for court funding which goes into effect this
month. Staff believes there is a sufficient balance of available funds per citation to offset costs
associated with the new service.

SUBJECT:  AWARD OF A PROFESSIONAL SERVICES AGREEMENT TO EVALUATE
  THE NEEDS FOR SEISMIC REHABILITATION OF CITY HALL IN THE
  AMOUNT OF $15,000 TO MELVYN GREEN & ASSOCIATES

DATE:  DECEMBER 14, 2010
_____________________________________________________________________________

The Issue

Should the City Council award a professional services agreement in the amount of $15,000 to
Melvyn Green & Associates to evaluate the needs for seismic rehabilitation of City Hall?

Background and Analysis

The City Council requested that staff evaluate the need for structural retrofits of City Hall due to
concerns with the aging building and its ability to withstand a major earthquake. City Hall is the
designated location for our Emergency Operations Center and the loss of City Hall would
dramatically hamper our ability to provide emergency services to our residents.

City Hall was constructed in 1954 and a seismic upgrade was performed in 1992. However, due to
findings from the 1994 Northridge Earthquake, building codes have been revised to reflect the
actual performance of various construction methods and materials during a seismic event. The
City’s structural engineer has reviewed the previous upgrade construction documents and is
particularly concerned with shearwalls throughout the building and the supporting columns below
the parking deck.

Staff contacted three local reputable structural engineering firms and received proposals from each
for the evaluation of City Hall – Structural Focus, Palos Verdes Engineering, and Mel Green and
Associates. The scope of work includes the evaluation of City Hall, Home Association Building,
and parking structure using current design criteria to locate seismic deficiencies and a cost estimate
to remedy any deficiencies. Please note that construction plans and specifications would need to be
created per a separate contract to perform the work.

CITY COUNCIL AGENDA
DECEMBER 14, 2010
  9
 Of the three proposals, staff felt that Mel Green and Associates had the best background and
approach to the project. He has performed similar reviews of public buildings such as ours,
including the Hermosa Beach Fire Station, and is a recognized expert in the field evidenced by his
many publications in the field.

There is $10,000 allocated in the current City budget. The additional $5,000 will be accounted for
in a year-end budget adjustment.

Alternatives Available to Council

The following alternatives are available to the City Council:

1.  Award a professional services agreement in the amount of $15,000 to Melvyn Green &
  Associates to evaluate the needs for seismic rehabilitation of City Hall.

2.  Decline to act.

Recommendation from Staff

Staff recommends that the Council award a professional services agreement in the amount of
$15,000 to Melvyn Green & Associates to evaluate the needs for seismic rehabilitation of City Hall.

Allan Rigg
Public Works Department

SUBJECT:  ADOPTION OF ORDINANCE 10-698; ADOPTING THE 2010 CALIFORNIA
  BUILDING CODE, THE 2010 CALIFORNIA RESIDENTIAL CODE, THE
  2010 CALIFORNIA ELECTRICAL CODE, THE 2010 CALIFORNIA
  MECHANICAL CODE, THE 2010 CALIFORNIA PLUMBING CODE, THE
  2010 CALIFORNIA ENERGY CODE, THE 2010 CALIFORNIA GREEN
  BUILDING CODE, THE 2010 CALIFORNIA HISTORICAL BUILDING
  CODE, THE 2010 CALIFORNIA EXISTING BUILDING CODE, THE 2010
  CALIFORNIA REFERENCED STANDARDS, THE 2009 INTERNATIONAL
  PROPERTY MAINTENANCE CODE, THE 2009 UNIFORM SWIMMING
  POOL, SPA, AND HOT TUB CODE, AND THE 2009 UNIFORM SOLAR
  ENERGY CODE

DATE:  DECEMBER 14, 2010

The Issue

Should the City Council adopt Ordinance 10-698; Adopting the 2010 California Building Code and
other Codes regulating construction activities?

Background and Analysis

On November 23, 2010 the City Council approved the introduction of Ordinance 10-698 adopting
the 2010 California Building Code and other Codes regulating construction activities. The public
hearing tonight is for the purposes of adopting the ordinance.

Every three years the California Building Standards Commission (BSC) updates the International
Codes governing construction practices in the State of California. Affected state agencies review
these codes, amend them, and the BSC adopts them in Title 24 of the California Code of
Regulations. After the State Code is published, every City and County throughout the state must
adopt the Codes, with an opportunity to include more stringent local amendments based on local
geological, topographical and/or climatic conditions.

CITY COUNCIL AGENDA
DECEMBER 14, 2010
  11
 On July 1, 2010 the State of California published and made available the 2010 Edition of the
California Code(s) of Regulations, Title 24 consisting of the following:

  1. The California Building Code
  2. The California Residential code
  3. The California Electrical Code
  4. The California Mechanical Code
  5. The California Plumbing Code
  6. The California Energy Code
  7. The California Historical Building Code
  8. The California Green Building Code
  9. The California Existing Building Code
  10. The California Referenced Standards

The following codes are published but not required by the state to adopt. These codes are called
appendix and provide language along with minimum guide lines for installations that are recognized
by the state. It is up to the local jurisdiction to adopt these appendices if the jurisdiction intends to
use them. It is recommended that the following appendixes be adopted.

  1. The California Building Code Appendix I; clarifies language in regards to patio covers for
  multi residential and commercial buildings, also adopted by HCD.
  2. The California Building Code Appendix J; Provides language and minimum guidelines for
  grading operations.
  3. The California Residential Code Appendix H; clarifies language in regards to for patio
  covers for Single Family Residents, also adopted by HCD.
  4. The California Residential Code Appendix O provides language along with installation
  guidelines for gray water systems.
  5. The California Plumbing Code Appendix G provides language along with installation
  guidelines for gray water systems.

The following codes are not published by the State but are recommended to be adopted by the local
jurisdiction:

  1. The 2009 International Property Maintenance Code
  2. The 2009 Uniform Swimming Pool, Spa and Hot Tub Code
  3. The 2009 Uniform Solar Energy Code.

Please note that the State allows local jurisdictions to make technical amendments or deletions to
the codes providing the amendments are equivalent to or more restrictive than those adopted. The
local agency must make an expressed finding that the amendments are necessary due to local
climatic, geological, or topographical conditions.

The City’s Building Official, Geologist, and the structural engineering plan reviewer have been
CITY COUNCIL AGENDA
DECEMBER 14, 2010
  12
 reviewing the Codes and found that the content of these Codes are very similar to the Codes
previously adopted by the City with the exception of, the 2010 California Green Building Code and
the 2010 California Residential Code. The Residential Codes are well written and clarify many
deficient areas of the Residential end of the building industry with much clearer language on the
Codes. However, the following amendments which were previously included in the City’s
Municipal Code should be reintroduced:

  Chapter 15.12.020  Administration (similar to existing Code)
  Chapter 15.12.030  Fees – (same as existing Code)
  Chapter 15.12.040  Liability – Includes agents under contract (similar to existing Code)
  Chapter 15.12.050  Maintenance Agreement – Requires a “Construction Site Maintenance
  Agreement” (same as existing Code)
  Chapter 15.12.060  Building Permit Expiration – 6 months initial, 6 months renewal at
  half fees (same as existing Code)
  Chapter 15.12.070  Underground Utilities – services must be undergrounded unless
  impractical (same as existing Code)
  Chapter 15.12.080  Aluminum wiring to be used in limited circumstances and with
  continuous inspection (same as existing Code)

When we last adopted codes in 2007 we adopted the California Fire Code. Due to changes
regarding the implementation of fire hazard severity zones by the State, we believe it is more
consistent to solely utilize the Los Angeles County Fire Code, which is adopted already within our
Municipal Code.

California Building Standards are applicable to all occupancies throughout California, whether or
not the local government takes an affirmative action to adopt those California Building Standards
and they become effective January 1, 2011. As we have been wrestling with how to address a
variety of Fire Code issues, we anticipate we will adopt Ordinance 10-698 on December 14, 2010,
which means that the amendments and appendices will not be effective until January 13, 2011. As
the amendments are essentially the same as the existing Code, and the appendices are rarely if ever
used, we are comfortable with the delay in the enforceability of both.

In order to adopt the latest California Codes, the City must follow the procedure set forth in Section
50022.3 of the Government Code. After first reading of the titles of the Ordinances, a public
hearing is scheduled by the City Council. The Ordinances may be adopted after the hearing.

Alternatives Available to Council

The following alternatives are available to the City Council:

1.  Open the public hearing, receive public input, close the public hearing and adopt Ordinance
  10-698 adopting the 2010 California Building Code and other Codes regulating construction
  activities.

CITY COUNCIL AGENDA
DECEMBER 14, 2010
  13
 2.  Open the public hearing, receive public input, close the public hearing and direct staff to
  make changes to Ordinance 10-698 for reintroduction at a future meeting

3.  Decline to act.

Recommendation from Staff

Staff recommends the Council adopt Ordinance 10-698 adopting the 2010 California Building Code
and other Codes regulating construction activities

Fiscal Impact

Building plan check and permit fees are paid to compensate the City for expenditures associated
with these activities. As the changes in the Codes are minor, the fees collected will continue to
match the expenditures, and there will be no net fiscal impact to the City.

SUBJECT:  PALOS VERDES GOLF CLUB 2011 OPERATING AND CAPITAL
  IMPROVEMENT BUDGETS

The Issue

Shall the City Council approve the 2011 Annual Operating and Capital Improvement budgets, along
with the specified dues increases, as proposed by the Palos Verdes Golf Club?

Background and Overview

The Concession Agreement with the Palos Verdes Golf Club (PVGC) stipulates that the Club shall
prepare and deliver to the City a comprehensive budget for the next succeeding calendar year,
together with a written request for approval by the City. The budget must include the estimated
income by source, expenditures by major category of expense, and any and all requests for major
capital expenditures or deferred maintenance items to be funded from the Club Improvement Fund.
In addition, the Club must secure the concurrence of the City Council for any fee increases. The
PVGC proposal was reviewed by the Council Liaison Committee (Mayor Humphrey,
Councilmember Perkins and City Manager Hoefgen) at a meeting on November 12, 2010.

The proposed 2011 Budget for the Palos Verdes Golf Club is one of transition as the Golf Club
works to fill available membership slots. As Council will recall, in September the PVGC received
authorization to increase the number of Regular Members from the prior maximum of 560 to the
new maximum of 600 members. PVGC General Manager Steve Hockett will provide an overview
of the Golf Club’s outreach efforts to date in filling the 40 recently created membership slots with
PVE residential property owners.

A copy of the proposed 2011 PVGC Budget is attached to this staff report. This budget has been
approved by the PVGC Board of Directors. Highlights of the proposed 2011 budget are provided
on the following page:

  •  Overall PVGC revenue is projected to increase by 3.08% in 2011. Total operating expenses
  are projected to increase by 2.4% in 2011.

CITY COUNCIL AGENDA
DECEMBER 14, 2010
  15
   •  The proposed budget assumes a 4% dues increase effective April 1, 2011. There would be
  no increase in green fees however.

  •  The proposed budget assumes 580 members (out of the 600 authorized) effective January 1,
  2011. Full membership at 600 members is anticipated by March 1, 2011. As of the release
  of this report, the Golf Club’s membership totals 575 Regular Members.

  •  The PVGC has made some special outreach to Terranea, and anticipates approximately
  $70,000 in additional revenue (primarily green fees) throughout 2011.

  •  The proposed budget incorporates 2% in performance based salary increases for PVGC
  employees, and an anticipated 10% increase in the cost of group health insurance rates.

  •  The capital budget includes continued investment in the Club totaling $236,000 in 2011 –
  with $11,500 allocated for a Hydro Geological Study for the feasibility of accessing
  underground water for irrigation purposes. Within the $236,000 capital budget, there is a
  significant placeholder budget in the amount of $64,870 available for other capital needs at
  the Club.

  •  The overall cash position of the Club returns to a more comfortable level of $451,866 at the
  end of 2011. This is a significant improvement as compared to a cash balance of $223,810
  at the beginning of 2010.

Dues Increase

In order to maintain services, the Golf Club is proposing an increase in membership dues of four
percent effective April 1, 2011. Council will recall that member dues increased by six percent
effective October 1, 2010 – shown below in the middle column. Dues for family members will
increase by $20 monthly along with comparable dues increases for other member categories:
  Effective  Effective  Effective
  01/01/10  10/01/10  04/01/11

    Regular Family (Resident)  $461  $489  $509
    Regular Single (Resident)  $360  $382  $397
    Senior Family (Resident)  $230  $244  $254
    Senior Single ( Resident)  $179  $190  $197
    Associate Family (Resident)  $146  $155  $161
    Associate Single ( Resident)  $ 98  $104  $108

PVGC Members have been advised of the recommended dues increase. As previously mentioned,
there is no proposed increase in green fees for any membership categories. The final attachments to
this report include a complete price sheet as well as a history of prior year dues increases at the Club
since 2000.

CITY COUNCIL AGENDA
DECEMBER 14, 2010
  16
 Summary

The Golf Club has a long history of realistic budgeting and conservative spending. In meeting with
PVGC representatives, it is clear that the PVGC is committed to maintaining a high level of service
to their members and will continue to proactively manage their budget to achieve desired results.

Alternatives Available to City Council

  1. Approve the 2011 Annual Budget and Dues Increases proposed by the Palos Verdes Golf
  Club. This would allow the Club to proceed in accordance with the plan approved by the
  Board of Directors and endorsed by the Council Liaison Committee.

  2. Do not approve the 2011 Annual Budget and Dues Increases proposed by the Palos Verdes
  Golf Club. This would require the Board of Directors to reformulate the budget for the
  upcoming year to address any concerns expressed by the City Council.

  3. Approve the 2011 Annual Budget and Dues Increases proposed by the Palos Verdes Golf
  Club subject to specified modifications. These would be as elaborated by the City Council.

Conclusions and Recommendations

It is recommended the City Council…..

  1. Approve the 2011 Operating Budget and Capital Improvement Budget proposed by the
  Palos Verdes Golf Club Board of Directors and endorsed by the Council Liaison Committee;
  and

  2. Approve the dues increases to take effect on April 1, 2011.

Budget Impact

The PVGC is a non-profit entity whose budget exists apart from the City. It pays an annual 10%
concession fee to the City, which the Golf Club is projecting to increase by approximately 1.5% in
2011 – for a total 2011 concession amount of $813,528. We will continue to monitor concession
payments and as part of the budget process will incorporate a conservative revenue projection for
concession payments in the 2011-12 budget.

SUBJECT:  RESOLUTION R10-28 ESTABLISHING MANAGEMENT AND
  CONFIDENTIAL EMPLOYEE COMPENSATION FOR FY 2010-11

DATE:  DECEMBER 14, 2010

ISSUE

Shall the City adopt Resolution R10-28 establishing Management and Confidential Employee
compensation for FY 2010-11?

BACKGROUND

Earlier this year, the City concluded negotiations with the Public Service Employees’ Group and the
Palos Verdes Estates’ Police Officers’ Association to establish compensation for those eligible
employees for the current fiscal year. As is customary, Management and Confidential employees
are provided with salary and benefit adjustments which mirror what is provided to the other
bargaining groups. The Management and Confidential group consists of the Assistant City
Manager, Police Chief, Police Captains, Financial Services Manager, Administrative Analyst,
Executive Assistant to the City Manager, and Secretary to the Police Chief,

The one-year agreement provides the following:

  1. A one-time stipend of $500 per full-time employee to be paid on Friday, December 17,
  2010.

  2. An increase of $75 per month ($1,105 total per month) to the City’s monthly
  contribution toward the medical insurance cap effective July 1, 2010.

Additionally, the employment agreement of the City Manager provides that the City Manager shall
receive the same insurance benefits as provided to other Department Heads of the City and the same
general cost of living adjustment as approved for other executive management employees of the
City.

 ALTERNATIVES AVAILABLE TO COUNCIL

CITY COUNCIL AGENDA
DECEMBER 14, 2010
  18
 1. The City Council may choose to adopt Resolution R10-28.
2. The City Council may choose not to adopt Resolution R10-28.
3. The City Council may postpone adoption of Resolution R10-28.

CONCLUSIONS AND RECOMMENDATION

It is recommended that the City Council adopt Resolution R10-28 establishing Management and
Confidential Employee compensation for FY 2010-11.

BUDGET IMPACT

The cost for this one-year agreement is $9,500, which represents an aggregate 0.75% increase in
total compensation for the Management and Confidential Employees and the City Manager.

   Agenda Item #:  10
  Meeting Date:  12/14/2010

TO:  MAYOR AND CITY COUNCILMEMBERS

FROM:  JOSEPH HOEFGEN, CITY MANAGER

SUBJECT:  MID YEAR STATUS REPORT ON THE FY 2010-11 WORK PROGRAM

DATE:  DECEMBER 14, 2010

Issue

Mid-Year Status report on FY 2010-11 Work Program.

Background and Analysis

On July 13, 2010, shortly following the City Council’s adoption of the 2010-11 Budget, I presented
a Work Program identifying major work activities occurring over the subsequent 12 months in City
Departments. As Council will remember, the purpose of the Work Program is to identify work
milestones and projected target dates as part of an overall strategy to manage the workload of each
of the departments.

While the Work Program captures many of the departments’ work activities, it is not a complete list
of all of our duties and responsibilities. The Work Program is intended to highlight certain projects
and work activities that require considerable time and resources throughout the year, and to reflect
work that has been added since the original Work Program was presented.

Now that we are at mid-point in the fiscal year, it is appropriate to review the progress to date
toward completion of the City’s Work Program. While certain dates have been adjusted, the
changes to the Work Program are, by and large, minimal compared to prior years. While the
detailed pages for each of the City’s Departments are attached to this report, the following two
pages provide highlights by department:

During the past six months, the City Manager’s Office has completed a number of priority projects
including coordination of labor discussions with employee groups resulting in a one-year term that
reflects the continued uncertainty of the economy and the State deficit that is now projected to
exceed $25 billion dollars over the next 18 months. While the recent passage of Proposition 22 has
provided a measure of security that did not previously exist, cities remain on guard for adverse
actions by the State of California.

CITY COUNCIL AGENDA
DECEMBER 14, 2010
  20
 Also in the City Manager’s Office, significant progress was made to update the City’s civil services
rules which have remained in effect without change since 1951. The net result will be up-to-date
Personnel Rules which we will be sharing with employees/employee groups after the first of the
year before final review, adoption, and implementation.

Considerable staff effort was spent working with the Palos Verdes Golf Club to finalize
membership changes at the PVGC to help ensure the Club’s fiscal sustainability and to ensure that
the needs of PVE residents were met. Additionally, while not anticipated in the original Work
Program, the City Manager’s Office spent considerable time getting up to speed on the potential
impacts resulting from possible changes in the airspace regulations at Long Beach Airport with a
City Council report in September 2010.

During the summer of 2010, the Police Department completed the testing and interviews for the
positions of Captain, Sergeant, and Corporal and continues to seek qualified candidates to fill
available Services Officer and Police Officer positions. Progress continues on efforts to
replace/upgrade the police radio system to increase coverage and reliability. The Disaster District
Plan took a major step forward with the acquisition and placement of six disaster supply containers
for use by emergency workers in PVE. The Department will continue to help recruit individuals to
serve as disaster service workers and Ham radio operators -- critical volunteer components of our
Disaster District Plan.

Additionally, in recent months, the Police Department developed schedules for the periodic
enforcement of vehicle and bicycle regulations to help ensure that enforcement occurs at key
locations throughout the community. Lastly, the Police Department continues to promote the very
popular PVE CARES Program which serves the needs of seniors in Palos Verdes Estates.

The City Clerk/Finance Department achieved a major milestone last summer with the launch of
the City’s new and improved web site (www.pvestates.org). In addition, City staff is now posting
all web page updates as opposed to having this work completed by an outside vendor. Like the
update of the web page, the City Clerk’s office is taking the lead on an update of the PVE
Municipal Code and the City Council recently held the first of what will be three or four workshops
to complete this project – the first comprehensive update since 1988. In terms of Risk
Management, staff received the Joint Powers Insurance Agency (JPIA) risk management audit and
is working to address the recommendations from the audit.

In early 2011, the Finance Department will be finalizing the Request for Proposals (RFP) for
auditing services as outlined in the original FY 2010-11 Work Program presented last July.
Additionally, within the next few weeks, the Finance Department will undertake a review of the
City’s PERS rates and determine the possibility of another lump sum contribution to reduce the
City’s public safety pension costs.

In the Planning and Public Works Department, a number of projects have been completed during
the past six months including the annual slurry seal and overlay work pursuant to the City’s multi-
year Pavement Management Program. The construction of the underground sewage pump station at
Via Barri is progressing and in the spring of 2011 the Rocky Point Road Pump Station will be under
construction as well. Additionally, the Planning/Public Works Department recently completed the
CITY COUNCIL AGENDA
DECEMBER 14, 2010
  21
 review of proposals received to perform a seismic analysis of City Hall (funded by the proceeds of
the Haag Estate) and this report is also on tonight’s agenda for Council review and action.

Planning/Public Works has taken on some additional projects including (1) reviewing traffic
calming options for the 500 to 700 blocks of Via del Monte to slow speeding traffic and improve
safety for area residents; and (2) Reviewing proposed revitalization plans for the Lunada Bay Plaza
and assisting with implementation, where possible within our existing resources. Both of these
additional projects have involved considerable interaction with the public to arrive at desired
results.

  # # #

In prior years, vacancies in key staff positions contributed to certain projects being carried forward
and not completed. However, with leadership positions in all departments now filled and limited
turnover, staff has been able to complete projects without significant delays.

Recommendation from Staff

As this report is informational in nature, there is no formal action required of the City Council.

 Mayor Humphrey said the ordinance was introduced and discussed at the November 23, 2010 City

Councilmember Goodhart asked that information on the new codes be communicated to PVE

NEW BUSINESS

PALOS VERDES GOLF CLUB  2011  ANNUAL  OPERATING  AND  CAPITAL
IMPROVEMENT BUDGETS

Councilmember Bird recused himself from the discussion and left the chamber as he is a current
member of the Golf Club.

City Manager Hoefgen reported that the Concession Agreement requires the Golf Club to prepare a
budget for review by the City prior to the start of the new budget year. 2011 will be a year of transition
for the Golf Club as they move to a fill the 40 new regular membership slots that were approved by the
City Council in September. There is a connection between the slots being filled and the financial
viability of the Golf Club. The budget projects a 3% revenue increase while the operating expenses are
projected to increase by 2.4%. The 2011 budget reflects a 4% dues increase effective April 1st. The
capital budget is close to $250,000. The Club is exploring the use of ground water to defray some of
the irrigation costs. Council Liaisons Humphrey and Perkins met with Club representatives in
November and are supportive of the proposed budget and dues increase.

Councilmember Goodhart asked about the ground water and who legally owns it. Manager Hoefgen
said the Golf Club has solicited a legal opinion and the City is in the process of reviewing the opinion.
The Club believes the City owns the rights to access the water. Councilmember Goodhart asked if that
is the case, why the City isn’t investigating the drilling of a well. Manager Hoefgen believed that the
Club and the City would be handling jointly. Mayor Humphrey said the legal opinion is still being
reviewed.

Mayor Pro Tem Rea said that the Malaga Cove groundwater research was paid for by the two water
districts. He wondered if they could be involved in the drilling and testing for the Golf Club.
Manager Hoefgen said that would be the intention once it is determined who owns the rights to the
water.

CITY COUNCIL
DECEMBER 14, 2010  3
 General Manager Steve Hockett reported that the Club intends to try to fill the additional 40 regular
membership slots that were approved by the Council with PVE resident property owners. The Club is
heavily marketing the reduced wait time for membership. There are currently 575 members. The first
41 people were contacted on the waiting list, aka AGMs, with a positive response from 26 of those. He
is seeing good trends and believes the membership issue will have a positive outcome.

George Manfredi, the out-going Club President, expressed his appreciation to the Council and City
staff for the cooperation the Club has received during this challenging year. The cooperation has eased
the burden to the Club’s Board of Directors. He complimented City Manager Hoefgen and said it was
a joy to work with him.

It was moved by Mayor Pro Tem Rea, seconded by Councilmember Perkins and unanimously
approved to approve the 2011 Operating Budget and Capital Improvement Budget proposed by the
Palos Verdes Golf Club Board of Directors and endorsed by the Council Liaison Committee; and
approve the dues increases to take effect on April 1, 2011. (4-0, Bird recused)

RESOLUTION R10-20 ESTABLISHING MANAGEMENT  AND  CONFIDENTIAL
EMPLOYEE COMPENSATION FOR FY 2010-11

City Manager Hoefgen said that negotiations between the City and Public Service Employees
Association and the Police Officers’ Association took place earlier in the year. The past practice for
the City has been to extend to the Management and Confidential Employees comparable changes in
compensation. This would provide the Management and Confidential Employees a one-time stipend
of $500 for each employee and an increase of $75 per month to the City’s contribution towards each
employee’s group health and dental program retroactive the July 2010. He also noted that any changes
in compensation or insurance benefits that the executive employees receive are also extended to the
City Manager per his employment agreement. The total one-year cost for these changes is $9,500 for
all Management and Confidential Employees.

Mayor Humphrey said the Council wishes they could do more for the employees for providing service
to the residents, but funds are not available to do so at this time.

It was moved Councilmember Goodhart, seconded by Councilmember Bird, and unanimously
approved to adopt Resolution R10-28 establishing Management and Confidential Employee
compensation for FY 2010-11.

STAFF REPORTS

City Manager’s Report

Mid-Year Status Report on FY 2010-11 Work Program

City Manager Hoefgen said the Work Program highlights significant work activities and projects for
the 12 month period ending June 30, 2011. The Work Program helps the Department Heads and the
CITY COUNCIL
DECEMBER 14, 2010  4
 City Manager to manage projects and track the progress of work and significant work activities
throughout the year. The City is midway through the current budget year and the Work Program is
updated at this midway point. In the City Manager’s office, Human Resources has been very busy
with negotiation and significant work has been done updating the Personnel Rules. HR has
coordinated with the Police Department for promotional positions and also worked on issuing an
RFP for insurance brokerage services. The airspace regulations around Long Beach airport and the
Golf Club membership issues also required significant allocation of resources. In the Police
Department there was significant progress made toward the replacement of the current radio system.
The Disaster District Program moved from a planning phase to implementation – the containers
have been placed at the school sites and stocked and the volunteer training is on-going. There were
several key promotions in the PD in the past six months and there are new strategies in place for
enforcing the bicycle and vehicle moving violations. In the City Clerks department the major
milestone was the completion of the new web page with the updates now being completed in-house.
The City Clerk is also working with the City Attorney to update the Municipal Code. The Finance
Department will be soliciting proposals for auditing services. Planning and Public Works has
completed approximately $1 million in slurry and overlay projects on the streets. Public Works is
also overseeing a planned rebuild of two sewer pumps stations. PW had handled the unexpected
Via del Monte traffic calming issues and the coordination and review of the Lunada Bay Plaza
improvements.

Councilmember Goodhart said there have been a lot of complaints at Traffic Safety Committee
meetings over the last many months regarding traffic enforcement. He believes that the PD has
been running understaffed, not by design, from the allowed 25 positions. He wondered what the
impact to the issue would be if the number of officers were increased – he asked how the evaluation
of the number of officers required occurs. He thought this would be a good item to discuss at the
Council retreat. Mayor Humphrey said it was a financial decision.

As the Work Program was presented as an informational report, Council received the report and did
not take action.
